done_when: When the one-by-one replay conflicts but the whole-branch merge (merge-tree of the replay baseline and the branch head onto main) is clean, close replays the part as one commit with that merged tree and continues; a real whole-branch conflict still refuses as today; new and existing repos get it on upgrade

known.title: Preserve earlier review rounds during the squash
Keep planning evidence from the worker's separate commit
Keep squashed follow-up fixes recognizable as built

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 3, Harm 4
Raise: Data loss
Case: normal use - a stacked part has been reviewed more than once before its parent merges.
The replacement commit has only the default-branch tip as a parent, so the earlier review-result commits disappear from the published branch. `review._history` in `src/forge/review.py:605` reads those snapshots from first-parent history; after the squash it can see only the latest snapshot. Earlier findings and dismissals therefore no longer reach the next review and can be raised again. A fresh clone cannot reconstruct those rounds from the branch. The coordinator's single-commit ruling did not address this history consumer.
findings.title: Preserve earlier review rounds during the squash

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Data loss
Case: normal use - the worker records `Before coding:` in the required empty commit, then makes a code commit with its proof list.
`review.commit_paragraph` in `src/forge/review.py:698` stops at the latest non-bookkeeping commit for this label, so it returns empty when the planning paragraph is in the earlier commit. The squash then removes that commit from branch history, leaving the next review and pull request without the planning evidence the coordinator required. Earlier `Ruling:`, `Declined:` and `Spotted:` lines can be lost for the same reason. The new test hides the planning case by putting `Before coding:` in the last code commit.
findings.title: Keep planning evidence from the worker's separate commit

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a follow-up fix has an intermediate replay conflict after its parent is squash-merged, while its final changes merge cleanly.
This replay path also handles stacked fixes. The new commit adds both the fix's state file and its product work, so `task.unbuilt_fix` at `src/forge/task.py:847` treats that commit as the start and excludes its work from the search. After a successful close, `forge land` consequently starts another build at `src/forge/land.py:102` instead of landing the ready fix.
findings.title: Keep squashed follow-up fixes recognizable as built

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - main gains a file while the stacked part is being developed.
The fixture creates `default_note.py` on main in `tests/test_close_replays_after_parent_review_commits.py:83`, but this test checks only `app.py` and `use.py`. An implementation that parents the replay commit on main while using the original part tree would delete that main-only file and still pass these assertions. The required merged-tree result therefore lacks effective proof; the command-level test needs to check the main-only content too.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_close_squashes_only_intermediate_conflicts

why: When a stacked part's parent has merged, close replays the part's own commits onto main one by one (git rebase in close._merge_default), so an early commit conflicts with later main edits of the same lines even when the whole-branch merge is clean; merging main into the branch never helps, and a client part looped 5 times on 19 Nov 2026
